Metrics.ElementText:
The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.
This is a Practising Surgery

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

Services.ServiceName: Alcohol addiction - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
Worried about your own or someone else’s alcohol or drug use? We offer free and confidential advice, support and treatment for people in Gloucestershire aged 18+.

We’ll talk about your concerns and make a plan together. This care plan will help you reduce or stop your drug or alcohol use – making sure you receive the right support at the right time for you. Help and advice for family, friends and carers on how best to support you during your recovery is also available.

At our service, you can get:

- Advice about your health and wellbeing
- Regular sessions with your personal keyworker
- A range of different support groups
- Women-only support and safe spaces in partnership with The Nelson Trust.
Gloucestershire
You can visit our service in person or contact us by phone or email. Any professional, such as a housing support worker, social worker, GP or nurse can also make a referral for you.

Services.ServiceName: Drug misuse - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
The service provides intervention for children and young people up to age 18 within the Northumberland area. Young people are supported to stop using substances, and to reduce the associated risks from substance misuse, both to themselves and their communities. They are also supported to achieve good physical and emotional health and wellbeing. 

Sorted can help:
- young people
- professionals and agencies working with young people

Young people up to 18 years old can access the service. We offer:
- 1-2-1 indivdual support
- strict confidentiality, whilst adhering to safegaurding requirements
- referral to other services, with the young person's permission. PLEASE NOTE: the young person must consent to any referral that is made.
- support to reduce use of substances/stop using substances
- multi-agency partnerships
- factual, unbiased information for young people about their substance use.

We will act with the best interests of the young person in mind.

It is free of charge, including any follow-up tests or appointments.

Healthwatch is your health and social care champion. If you use GPs and hospitals, dentists, pharmacies, care homes or other support services, we want to hear about your experiences.

As an independent statutory body, we have the power to make sure NHS leaders and other decision makers listen to your feedback and improve standards of care.

We can also help you to reliable and trustworthy information and advice. Last year, we helped nearly a million people like you to have your say and get the support you need.

Wherever you live in England, you will have a local Healthwatch nearby (there are over 150 across the country). We are here to listen to the issues that really matter to local communities and to hear about your experiences of using health and social care services.

We are entirely independent and impartial, and any information you share with us is confidential. Healthwatch uses your feedback to better understand the challenges facing the NHS and other care providers nationally, to make sure your experiences improve health and care services for everyone.

We can also help you to get the information and advice you need to make the right decisions for you and to get the support you deserve.

Services.ServiceName: Alcohol addiction - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText: Drug and or Alcohol misuse may be happening in your home or affecting someone close to you. You may feel alone, unable to cope, frightened, angry or confused. However, you are not to blame. Families are often crucial to recovery and Hetty’s can offer you strength to feel you can cope better. Support groups and 1-2-1 support available.

- Support Line: 08000 850 941, 9am- 6pm, Monday to Friday  
- Text Support: 07896 228 547,  9am-6pm  
- Admin line: 01623 643 476  
- Webchat available
Nottinghamshire

GsdServices.ServiceName: Alcohol addiction - support for family and friends

Services.ServiceName: Alcohol addiction - support for family and friends

Metrics.ElementText:
Our services help young people in Medway and surrounding areas who are worried about their use of alcohol or drugs, or concerned about how substance abuse is affecting another young person. 

A young person has a choice on: 
• Where they are seen 
• Being seen on their own or with some one you trust
• Choice of a male or female worker 

The service we provide is strictly confidential. We will only talk with other agencies if we are worried about your safety. If we do this, we will always tell you why.
Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm
Medway and West Kent
Self referral or via other agency

Metrics.ElementText:
Everyone’s journey is different. Whether you want to reduce your drug or alcohol use, use in a safer way, or work towards recovery, our experienced team are here to listen and offer confidential support. We’ll work with you to find the right help, at your pace and on your terms.  

We’re a partnership between Turning Point, Double Impact and Framework, allowing us to offer joined-up, non-judgemental and reliable advice and support. Our support is free, and available to all people living in North East Lincolnshire.
Monday 9 - 5, Tuesday 9 - 5, Wednesday 9 - 7, Thursday 9 - 5, Friday 9 - 5
North East Lincolnshire
Online, phone, in person

Resolve is a free-to-access adult drug and alcohol treatment service, delivering a range of services helping people break the cycle of alcohol and drug misuse.

Lincolnshire Recovery Partnership is a free and confidential service for people in Lincolnshire who want support with their drug and alcohol use.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.
This is a visiting/mobile service

Services.ServiceName: Mental health services for alcohol addiction

Metrics.ElementText:
Cranstoun Derby is an adult (aged 18+) drug and alcohol treatment service. The service works with all levels of drug and alcohol misuse from legal highs through to cannabis and cocaine, as well as heroin and crack use.  Cranstoun Derby also offers a Prescription Only Medication service (POMs) as well as: 
• intensive structured 1-to-1 and non-structured interventions  
• a mix of high and low intensity levels together with a specialist prescribing programme  
• an enhanced needle exchange programme  
• 1-to-1 keyworking, care planning and support  
• 1-to-1 structured care planned treatment and risk assessment for high risk service users  
• specialist health screening, Hepatitis C and HIV testing  
• community-based detoxification services  
• relapse prevention work alongside prescribing interventions
Monday 9.00am - 5.00pm, Tuesday 12.00pm - 5.00pm, Wednesday 9.00am - 8.00pm, Thursday 9.00am - 5.00pm, Friday 9.00am - 5.00pm
Derby City

This service accepts referrals  for drug and alcohol treatment - via Dropin, the website,  telephone, referral form emailed to service. Service users who require drug treatment directly on release from custody are referred via the prison healthcare Team and those who are given a court ordered Drug Rehabilitation Requirement (DRR) or Alcohol Treatment Requiement (ATR) will have appointments arranged by our criminal Justice team alongside preobation.
Cranstoun Derby deliver services across Derby City at various community locations.  Please contact the service for more details and a community venue that may better suit your needs.

The Forward Trust’s Essex service offers dedicated abstinence-based recovery pathways for individuals and families affected by drug and alcohol use, delivered through two SHARP programmes at Wickford and Braintree. Alongside abstinence pathways, we offer a suite of specialist interventions designed to meet people wherever they are in their recovery:
·  Brink of Change - a 6-week CBT-based programme consisting of OST-focused sessions and psychoeducational workshops.

·  Addiction counselling - a therapeutic space for individuals ready to explore their relationship with substances.
·  M-PACT - a structured programme supporting families affected by parental substance use.

Together, these services create a flexible, person-centred offer that empowers individuals and families to move forward with clarity, confidence, and the right level of support.

How we can help
We're here for adults in Luton who are struggling with alcohol and/or drug use. We'll listen to your needs and help you set goals so we can tailor your support. We believe everyone has the ability to change, and we're here to help you do it.

Alcohol
People use alcohol for different reasons – to be sociable, to relieve stress, cope with anxiety, and many other reasons. However, your drinking may be affecting you in ways you may not realise. You have the potential to change your drinking. We are here to help you achieve it. 

Drugs
We offer free and confidential advice and information around drugs. Whether you want to reduce your drug use or stop altogether, we're here for you.
We have a needle exchange programme and can offer advice about safer injecting. We also offer free naloxone and training on how to use it.

Contact us
If you'd like to get in touch, the best way would be to give us a call on 0800 054 6603.  You can find out more about what we do and ask any questions you might have. Don't forget to follow us on social media to see what we're up to.

Metrics.ElementText:
Recharge is a young persons support scheme based in Telford. 

We are here to offer you confidential support with drug or alcohol use. Age 12-21
10am - 4pm
Telford and Wrekin
Contact Recharge for easy referral

We are a user led abstinence based group, which means we agree collectively to reduce, but ultimately stop the use of cannabis, spice and legal highs within our membership.
 
We recognise the damage our drug misuse can do to ourselves and those around us and we choose to seek help from others who have recovered successfully from serious addictions. We have no affiliation to other mutual aid groups such as NA (Narcotics Anonymous) and SMART (Self Management and Recovery Training) but we do support and commend their work. We often refer our members to both meetings and others. We strongly believe that no one system works for everyone and we encourage our members to experience and embrace many different recovery systems, activities and communities.

We are not a cannabis appreciation society and we do not advocate legalisation. We do however acknowledge the particular CBD health benefits and call for greater and more transparent research. Similarly we recognise the failure of subsequent governments to sufficiently support appropriate treatment and recovery programmes.

We have achieved many levels of success within our membership, our groups have produced and maintained many years of clean-time. We have done this by creating a series of local meetings in a safe, confidential, non-judgmental and supportive environment, where members can rebuild their lives together.
Website is available 24/7. Call or text for details of group times.
West Yorkshire
Self referral or via other professionals.

Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. The Forward Trust’s Essex service offers dedicated abstinence-based recovery pathways for individuals and families affected by drug and alcohol use, delivered through two SHARP programmes at Wickford and Braintree. Alongside abstinence pathways, we offer a suite of specialist interventions designed to meet people wherever they are in their recovery:
·  Brink of Change - a 6-week CBT-based programme consisting of OST-focused sessions and psychoeducational workshops.

·  Addiction counselling - a therapeutic space for individuals ready to explore their relationship with substances.
·  M-PACT - a structured programme supporting families affected by parental substance use.

Together, these services create a flexible, person-centred offer that empowers individuals and families to move forward with clarity, confidence, and the right level of support.

The Bridges - Hull is a residential rehabilitation in the heart of Hull owned by The Forward Trust. For over 20 years, the service has provided residential care and treatment for people with drug and/or alcohol issues, helping to change the lives of hundreds of individuals.

The research-led treatment approach ensures that The Bridges is able to support every client on their recovery journey - both individually and as a group.

Metrics.ElementText:
Change Grow Live Manchester work with anyone looking to make positive changes related to drug & alcohol use. We approach treatment with an open mind, free from judgement. If your goals don't include treatment and recovery, but you do want to reduce the harmful impacts of drug & alcohol use, we can help with this too.  

Change Grow Live are a national organisation, with the aim to help people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals and live life to its full potential. In Manchester, we offer support with harm reduction, needle exchange, housing, criminal justice, employment, education & training and homeless outreach. We have links with other services, including a smoking addiction service also under the Change Grow Live umbrella, called Be Smoke Free, and we offer a service which works specifically with young people, called Eclypse. We work with Emerging Futures and Acorn to deliver our psychosocial intervention groups and after-treatment care, and LGBT Foundation to provide specialist support related to LGBTQ+ issues for those in treatment. 

Change Grow Live's teams work in partnership with service users to assess their requirements and to plan individual treatment plans and support that will help service users to address their problems and achieve their personal goals.

We provide a full range of treatment and recovery interventions for people who require services for their drug or alcohol use. We do this by providing:

- Initial assessment to work out what support will benefit you
- Brief interventions (including harm reduction advice and support over the phone)
- Medically assisted treatment (MAT)
- Support sessions with recovery coordinators and engagement workers – one-to-one and in small groups
- Second opinions when requested by a GP
- Community detox
- Referral for in-patient detox
- Links to rehab clinics
- Peer Support groups – informal drop-ins, and structured group programmes
- Health assessments
- Blood-borne virus (BBV) tests and treatment - HIV, Hep B and Hep C
- Hep B vaccinations
- Needle Syringe Programmes (AKA needle exchange)


We also deliver free online training to professionals on topics related to drug & alcohol use, which you can find on our Eventbrite page:  https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/cc/adult-drug-alcohol-training-for-professionals-2132019
Monday to Friday, 9am – 5pm.   Some evening openings available – please ring 0161 823 6306 for details.

Metrics.ElementText:
Change Grow Live Manchester work with anyone looking to make positive changes related to drug & alcohol use. We approach treatment with an open mind, free from judgement. If your goals don't include treatment and recovery, but you do want to reduce the harmful impacts of drug & alcohol use, we can help with this too.  

Change Grow Live are a national organisation, with the aim to help people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals and live life to its full potential. In Manchester, we offer support with harm reduction, needle exchange, housing, criminal justice, employment, education & training and homeless outreach. We have links with other services, including a smoking addiction service also under the Change Grow Live umbrella, called Be Smoke Free, and we offer a service which works specifically with young people, called Eclypse. We work with Emerging Futures and Acorn to deliver our psychosocial intervention groups and after-treatment care, and LGBT Foundation to provide specialist support related to LGBTQ+ issues for those in treatment. 

Change Grow Live's teams work in partnership with service users to assess their requirements and to plan individual treatment plans and support that will help service users to address their problems and achieve their personal goals.

We provide a full range of treatment and recovery interventions for people who require services for their drug or alcohol use. We do this by providing:

- Initial assessment to work out what support will benefit you
- Brief interventions (including harm reduction advice and support over the phone)
- Medically assisted treatment (MAT)
- Support sessions with recovery coordinators and engagement workers – one-to-one and in small groups
- Second opinions when requested by a GP
- Community detox
- Referral for in-patient detox
- Links to rehab clinics
- Peer Support groups – informal drop-ins, and structured group programmes
- Health assessments
- Blood-borne virus (BBV) tests and treatment - HIV, Hep B and Hep C
- Hep B vaccinations
- Needle Syringe Programmes (AKA needle exchange)


We also deliver free online training to professionals on topics related to drug & alcohol use, which you can find on our Eventbrite page:  https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/cc/adult-drug-alcohol-training-for-professionals-2132019
Monday to Friday, 9am – 5pm.   Some evening openings available – please ring 0161 823 6306 for details.
Manchester

The Forward Trust’s Essex service offers dedicated abstinence-based recovery pathways for individuals and families affected by drug and alcohol use, delivered through two SHARP programmes at Wickford and Braintree. These programmes provide structured, therapeutic support that helps people rebuild stability, confidence, and long-term wellbeing.

Alongside abstinence pathways, we offer a suite of specialist interventions designed to meet people wherever they are in their recovery:
·  Brink of Change - a 6-week CBT-based programme consisting of OST-focused sessions and psychoeducational workshops.
·  Non-addiction counselling - emotional and psychological support delivered by trainee counsellors.
·  Addiction counselling - a therapeutic space for individuals ready to explore their relationship with substances.
·  M-PACT - a structured programme supporting families affected by parental substance use.

Together, these services create a flexible, person-centred offer that empowers individuals and families to move forward with clarity, confidence, and the right level of support.

value.OrganisationName: Southampton SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist Service

Metrics.ElementText:
The SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist Service offers teaching group sessions in the community, home teaching visits and parent training courses for young children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) aged 0-3 years; who are delayed in at least two areas of development

We support children and families in Southampton who meet the following eligibility criteria:
·  The family live in the Southampton local authority area, 
·  The child is aged 0-3 years, 
·  The child’s development is delayed by at least six months in two or more areas of development, 
·  Parental consent has been obtained, 
·  The child’s parent/carer must be available to meet the SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist on a regular basis, 
· Note: If a child attends an early years setting for more than 15 hours a week, this may affect the type of support that the SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist is able to offer.

SEND & Portage Early Years Stay and Play session: 
Upon receipt of a referral a Senior SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist will contact the family to arrange an initial home visit.

If the service is felt to be appropriate then this information will be communicated to the family during the initial home visit and followed up with a letter to the referrer.

SEND & Portage Early Years specialist teaching sessions: 
The main focus of the groups will be communication, requesting, making choices, shared attention and turn taking. The group will follow the same routine each week which will include:
·  Arrival activity, 
·  Welcome song & Makaton sign, 
·  Attention activity, 
·  Modelling and practicing focus of the week, 
·  Messy play/free play, 
·  Singing, 
·  Questions, 
·  These groups are an opportunity for parents to be actively involved in their child’s play and to practice new strategies alongside the SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist.

SEND & Portage Early Years home teaching sessions: 
Families receive a weekly home teaching session from their Portage teacher, usually 6-8 visits.

This may include: 
·  Assessment of the child’s strengths and the areas that they find difficult, 
·  Learning through play in partnership with a parent/carer, 
·  Advice on pre-schools/early years settings and on the support that the child may need when they start at a setting, 
·  Signposting to other services.
Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm (term-time only).
Southampton

We support children and families in Southampton who meet the following eligibility criteria:
- The family live in the Southampton local authority area.
- The child is aged 0– 3 years
- The child’s development is delayed by at least 6 months in two or more areas of development.
- Parental consent has been obtained.
- The child’s parent/carer must be available to meet the Portage teacher on a regular basis.

What training do we have?  All SEND & Portage Early Years Specialists have:·  Foundation degree level qualifications in child development, ·  Significant experience of working within Early Years, ·  Significant experience of Special Educational Needs, ·  Significant experience of working with families, ·  Completed Portage Workshop, ·  Staff receive on-going training through the National Portage Development training program, as well as through Southampton City Council’s workforce development programme.  When necessary, we seek and provide additional training based on needs identified by the SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist, relating to working with children with specific special educational needs and disabilities.  How do we communicate with service users and how are they involved in decision?  Parents/carers and children are partners in all aspects of the SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist Service delivery.  All sessions in the home or at group includes both adult and child-led activities so that parents/carers and children have the opportunity to lead and influence the play and learning that takes place.  SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist Service will take into consideration the child’s likes and dislikes, the family’s day-to-day lives and their aspirations for their child, these are all included in the planning of each play session.  If the service is working with a family where by English is not their first language, they may ask if there’s a family member or friend who could act as a translator. If there isn’t anyone or the family don’t feel comfortable with this, employing a translator would be considered.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.
This is a Practising Surgery

Services.ServiceName: Rape and sexual assault referral centre

Metrics.ElementText: Available 24 hours, call for advice or to make an appointment.

Sexual assault referral centres offer medical, practical and emotional support to anyone who has been sexually assaulted or raped. They have specially trained pediatrician / Forensic Nurse Examiners (FNE)  and support workers to care for you.
In an emergency you should always call 999. If you are unable to safely talk to the operator answering your 999 call, press 55 on your handset to let them know you are there.
Other

The Treetops Centre Sexual Assault Referral Centre (SARC) is based in a discreet and secure location in Portsmouth. All our staff are specially trained to provide sensitive and well informed support in a non-judgmental manner and will ensure you are treated with dignity and respect at all times.

We can provide a supportive environment for anyone of any gender who has experienced rape or sexual assault. We will provide information and support on the choice of whether or not to report the assault to the police.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

Services.ServiceName: Mental health services for alcohol addiction

Metrics.ElementText:
Cranstoun Derby is an adult (aged 18+) drug and alcohol treatment service. The service works with all levels of drug and alcohol misuse from legal highs through to cannabis and cocaine, as well as heroin and crack use.  Cranstoun Derby also offers a Prescription Only Medication service (POMs) as well as: 
• intensive structured 1-to-1 and non-structured interventions  
• a mix of high and low intensity levels together with a specialist prescribing programme  
• an enhanced needle exchange programme

Metrics.ElementText:
Beyond Dementia is a registered charity founded in 1990, in response to a locally identified need for support for people living with dementia and their Carers. The aim of Beyond Dementia is to provide a range of flexible services to support people with Alzheimer’s Disease and other dementias, and their Carers.

Beyond Dementia works closely with the Avon  & Wiltshire Mental Health Care NHS Trust, Department of Adult and Community Services and Primary Care Trusts. We are now registered and inspected as a Domiciliary Care Service Provider and also run day clubs and a wide range of community activity groups, including singing, art, exercise, and outdoor nature groups.  Our dementia advisers provide information, advice and support from point of diagnosis and stay in touch with families so they have a named contact for ongoing support. Beyond Dementia is the main specialist provider of care for people with mild to moderate dementia in Wiltshire, assisting them to maintain as much independence and control over their lives as possible.

We work alongside Carers throughout the course of the illness by providing information and emotional support. Services for family carers include peer support groups and training courses.  We reflect client individuality by responding with flexible services inside and outside the home, 7 days a week.

We offer free, impartial, and confidential information, advice and support on Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) for children and young people aged 0 - 25, their families, and professionals across Hertfordshire.

Our service helps families navigate the SEND system, understand their rights, make informed choices, and feel empowered when making decisions about education, health and social care. We aim to strengthen engagement and communication between families, schools, the local authority and other agencies to help secure the best possible outcomes for children and young people.
